subject.title: clawhub install does not register skill hooks automatically

question: Should ClawHub automatically register skill-provided OpenClaw hooks during install/update, and what consent, scanner disclosure, and gateway targeting contract must be required before that happens?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but unconditional registration would cross a security boundary by activating publisher-controlled hook behavior during install without an established policy or runtime handoff contract.

options.title: Design consent-gated registration first
options.body: Define hook metadata, scanner disclosure, allowed event/type policy, explicit user approval, gateway target/restart behavior, and then implement install/update registration against that contract.

options.title: Keep manual registration for now
options.body: Document the manual `openclaw plugins install` path and keep `clawhub install` limited to copying skills until OpenClaw owns a native ClawHub hook install API.

options.title: Approve unconditional auto-registration
options.body: Install/update would register discovered hooks automatically, but this accepts the risk of activating publisher-controlled behavior without a new consent and disclosure boundary.

recommendation.title: Design consent-gated registration first
recommendation.body: Define hook metadata, scanner disclosure, allowed event/type policy, explicit user approval, gateway target/restart behavior, and then implement install/update registration against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest history match for the current CLI, metadata, and docs boundary that needs the maintainer decision.
